title: Displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector using quantum tomography of photon orbital angular momentum states
authors: Haorong Wu, Xilong Fan, Lixiang Chen
abstract: Gravitational waves (GWs) induce quantum transitions between photon orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) states with amplitudes $α_{\pm}$. Exploiting this effect, we present a displacement-noise-free detection framework that extracts GW information from the OAM Hilbert space. Parametrized quantum state tomography of the GW-induced OAM sidebands enables a single V-shaped detector to resolve all seven wave parameters: the frequency, propagation direction, two polarization amplitudes, and initial phase of each polarization. Direct detection of the sidebands yields a weak signal of approximately $10^{-15}\,\mathrm{W}$. We therefore introduce a stronger reference state $r |0>_{\mathrm{P}}$, with $r=0.01$, to enhance the detected signal. For an arm length of $L=4\,\mathrm{m}$, $N=160$ round trips, a paraxial parameter of $γ=0.1$, an incident light power of $P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10\,\mathrm{kW}$, a wavelength of $λ_{\mathrm{opt}}=1064\,\mathrm{nm}$, and GW amplitudes of $A=10^{-18}$, we estimate sideband transition amplitudes of $|α_{\pm}|\sim10^{-10}$ and signal powers of order $1\,\mathrm{nW}$, scaling as $P_{\mathrm{BS}}α_{\pm}\propto P_{\mathrm{BS}}ANLγ/λ_{\mathrm{opt}}$. The shot-noise-limited sensitivity floor is $S^{1/2}_n=1.6\times10^{-20}\,\mathrm{Hz}^{-1/2}$. Because the scheme measures OAM transition amplitudes rather than differential arm lengths, it is intrinsically free from displacement noise and provides a broadband probe of GWs, specifically bridging the $0.1$--$10\,\mathrm{Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.
summary: This paper proposes a novel, displacement-noise-free gravitational-wave detector that reads out GW signals by measuring quantum transitions in the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) states of photons. By employing quantum state tomography and a V-shaped interferometer, the scheme can resolve multiple GW parameters and is theoretically capable of bridging the critical $0.1-10 	ext{ Hz}$ frequency gap for detection.
main_problem: To develop a gravitational-wave (GW) detector that is immune to displacement noise by extracting GW information from the quantum transitions occurring in the Orbital Angular Momentum (OAM) states of photons.
main_result: The proposed V-shaped detector framework can resolve all seven GW wave parameters and provides a broadband probe capable of bridging the $0.1-10 	ext{ Hz}$ mid-frequency gap.
method: The method employs parametrized quantum state tomography on the OAM sidebands induced by GWs, enhancing the signal using a strong reference state to overcome direct detection limits.
model_or_system: The system uses photons whose OAM states undergo quantum transitions ($\alpha_{\pm}$) when passing through a region perturbed by a passing gravitational wave. The detection relies on measuring these transitions using a V-shaped interferometer geometry.
key_observables: The measured quantities are the projected state powers ($M_{P1}$ to $M_{P4}$), which are used to reconstruct the complex OAM transition amplitudes ($\alpha_P^\pm$) and ultimately the GW parameters ($	heta, \phi, 	ilde{A}_	imes, 	ilde{A}_+$).
important_parameters: Key parameters include the incident power ($P_{\mathrm{BS}}=10 	ext{ kW}$), arm length ($L=4 	ext{ m}$), number of round trips ($N=160$), and the reference state strength ($r=0.01$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the signal duration is much longer than the optical storage time ($t_d \gg 2NL$) and utilizes the paraxial approximation ($\gamma \ll 1$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the detector components (PM, PRM, BS, MZI, MP, PDs) for the two arms. Figure 2 shows the balanced signal powers ($	ext{R}_P$ and $	ext{I}_P$) versus GW frequency. Figure 3 compares the shot-noise-limited strain sensitivities for various configurations.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the physical mechanism of GW interaction with OAM states. It then details the quantum tomography measurement scheme, including signal enhancement and noise cancellation techniques. Finally, it derives the sensitivity floor and demonstrates the broadband capability of the detector.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to quantum optics and open quantum systems because it proposes using structured light (OAM states) and quantum measurement techniques (tomography) to sense extremely weak, non-linear physical perturbations (GWs), moving beyond standard linear interferometry.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of the proposed GW detector. Ab- breviations: phase modulator (PM), power recycling mir- ror (PRM), beamsplitter (BS), Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI), mode projector (MP), photodetector (PD). Solid black squares indicate breaks in the macroscopic arms. The states selected by the MPs and measured by the corresponding PDs are listed at the lower left.

FIG. 2. Balanced signal powers RP and IP at t = 0 as func- tions of GW frequency. Their magnitudes reach the nanowatt level at low frequencies. The incident power is PBS = 10 kW; the remaining parameters are specified in the main text.

FIG. 3. Shot-noise-limited strain sensitivities of the pro- posed detector for four configurations. Blue solid: L = 4 m, N = 160, PBS = 10 kW, and γ = 0.1. Orange dashed: L = 40 m, N = 160, PBS = 10 kW, and γ = 0.01. Green dash- dotted: L = 4 m, N = 16000, PBS = 100 W, and γ = 0.1. Purple dotted: L = 4 m, N = 16000, PBS = 1 kW, and γ = 0.1. Increasing the effective interaction time improves the low-frequency sensitivity at the expense of bandwidth, while increasing the incident power further reduces the shot-noise floor. The purple curve represents an idealized high-power benchmark. Other parameters are specified in the main text.

FIG. 4. Antenna patterns for the ×-polarized GW. (a) |F A ×,1,Re| exhibits spatial nulls at θ = 0 as well as ϕ = 0 and π. The azimuthal nulls (ϕ) are covered by the complementary geometry of (b) |F A ×,1,Im|, while the polar nulls (θ) are covered by (c) |F B ×,1,Re|. The pattern for (d) |F B ×,1,Im| provides additional complex angular dependence. Together, these patterns ensure comprehensive angular sensitivity.
